outlooks.summary: Severe storms are likely today across parts of the Great Plains from Iowa to Oklahoma and the Texas Panhandle, and from the mid Mississippi Valley southeastward into the Southeast.

sections.title: Southern and Central Plains/Lower Missouri Valley
sections.text: An upper-level ridge will move eastward across the mid Mississippi Valley and Great Lakes region today as southwest mid-level flow remains over the Great Plains. At the surface, a cold front will move southward across parts of the southern and central Plains as a low moves into the lower to mid Missouri Valley. By afternoon, the position of the front is forecast to be located from the eastern Texas Panhandle northeastward into northwest Oklahoma, east-central Kansas and far southeast Nebraska. Convection appears likely to first initiate along the front from the eastern Texas Panhandle into southern Kansas during the late afternoon. Strong to extreme instability with MLCAPE values in the 3000 to 5000 J/kg range combined with moderate deep-layer shear, will be favorable for supercell development. RAP forecast soundings from far northwest Oklahoma into southern Kansas late this afternoon just ahead of the front have 700 to 500 mb lapse rates of 8.0 to 8.5 C/km suggesting very large hail will be possible with the stronger supercells. Wind damage along with an isolated tornado threat will also be possible with supercells. As storms congeal into an MCS from Oklahoma into southeast Kansas

sections.title: Mid Mississippi and Tennessee Valleys into the Southeast
sections.text: Northwest mid-level flow will be in place today from the Mid Mississippi Valley southeastward into parts of the Southeast. At the surface, an outflow boundary will be located across the northern Gulf Coast States this morning. This outflow boundary will be important as to where the strongest instability develops this afternoon. The current thinking is that the moist airmass will retreat northward into western Tennessee with a northwest to southeast gradient of instability setting up from the mid Mississippi Valley southeastward into the Tennessee Valley. Convection is forecast to move southeastward along the instability gradient late this morning. This convection will probably develop a wind-damage threat early this afternoon as low-level lapse rates steepen. Additional thunderstorms may develop from the instability gradient southward across the warm sector this afternoon. Any storms that can organize a cold pool will likely have wind-damage potential. At this time, uncertainty is too great concerning the mesoscale details to warrant adding an enhanced risk area. ..Broyles/Squitieri.. 06/22/2019

outlooks.summary: Scattered thunderstorms should produce severe weather over parts of the central and southern Plains today, as well as from the mid Mississippi Valley across parts of the Southeast.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: In mid/upper levels, mean troughing and associated cyclonic flow will prevail over the western CONUS, while ridging extends from the western Gulf across the upper Great Lakes to Hudson Bay. East of the ridge, northwesterly flow aloft will prevail. West of the ridge, expect southwesterly mid/upper winds. Embedded within those winds will be several convectively generated or reinforced vorticity maxima, including one now moving southeastward over central IL. That perturbation should move across the south-central Appalachians around 00Z then offshore from the Carolinas about 06Z. An MCV initially over east-central KS -- not well-resolved yet by most progs initialized at and since 06Z -- should cross MO then turn southeastward over the lower OH Valley region through this evening. Another MCV -- evident over the southern Hill Country of TX -- should eject northeastward across the Red River toward south-central/Southeastern OK around 00Z, then over the Ozarks overnight. In the western cyclonic-flow regime, two closed cyclones were apparent in moisture-channel imagery: 1. Centered over extreme southern SK, and forecast to broaden while moving northward over eastern SK through the period. 2

sections.title: Southern/central Plains
sections.text: Three primary convective regimes are evident through the period, each mainly active this afternoon into evening. These are not hard-edged, and some spatial overlap is likely: 1. Scattered thunderstorms, both discrete and clusters, developing in the warm sector across north TX, central/eastern OK and southeastern KS, ahead of the ejecting MCV. Mainly multicell modes are likely, amidst relatively weak deep shear and low-level flow compared to the other two areas, though transient supercellular characteristics cannot be ruled out. 2. Convection developing in relatively maximized low-level convergence near the dryline and front, in a corridor from northwest TX across the eastern TX Panhandle, western/northern OK, and central/northeastern KS to parts of IA. Both multicell and heavy-precip supercell modes are expected in this regime. The eastern parts of this regime may blend into the first one noted above. 3. Post-frontal upslope activity forming this afternoon over the higher terrain of CO near and east of I-25 and moving east-northeastward across the central High Plains into strong shear but marginal buoyancy. sections.title: Mid Mississippi Valley to Southeast
sections.text: Clusters of thunderstorms should focus damaging-wind and isolated hail potential in this swath episodically throughout the period. The outflow-modulated warm-frontal corridor will foster an instability/ buoyancy gradient aligned northwest-southeast with the winds aloft. Enhanced wind potential may develop on the mesoscale with any complex than can organize a sufficiently robust cold pool while following the baroclinic zone southeastward, and also, while producing enough forced ascent to overcome CINH related to the gradual poleward decrease in surface-based instability. RAOBs and forecast soundings have sampled an EML plume in midlevels near the baroclinic zone, in support of favorable buoyancy when juxtaposed atop rich low-level moisture. One candidate for damaging-wind risk is an area of initially non-severe thunderstorms located over the lower Ohio Valley. This activity is fueled by an elevated warm/moist-advection layer atop the extensive cold pool from yesterday's and this mornings MCS that has moved offshore from the Carolinas. outlooks.summary: Clusters of thunderstorms should produce severe weather over parts of the central and southern Plains today, as well as from the mid Mississippi Valley across parts of the Southeast.

sections.title: Southeast States
sections.text: A long-lived MCS is currently over middle/east TN, with a general weakening trend noted in the past few hours. Given the mesoscale organization and large established cold-pool, it is likely that convection will re-intensify along the leading edge by mid-afternoon as the storms track across the Appalachians. The air mass downstream of the activity is rapidly heating/destabilizing with afternoon MLCAPE values expected to exceed 2000 J/kg. Forecast soundings also show sufficient west-northwesterly mid level winds to organize convection into bowing segments. Damaging winds appear to be the main risk with these storms, and have upgraded portions of western NC and much of SC to ENH risk for later today. It is unclear how the convection will evolve farther west over GA/AL. Weaker flow aloft will be offset by stronger CAPE values and steep low-level lapse rates. Scattered thunderstorms are expected to redevelop along the western flank of the remnant MCS over TN and sag into the region, with isolated storms forming farther south. Any of these storms will pose a risk of locally damaging wind gusts.

sections.title: TX/Southeast OK/Western AR
sections.text: Satellite/radar loops show an MCV over central TX drifting slowly northeastward. A consensus of 12z guidance shows thunderstorm development occurring in vicinity of this system by mid-afternoon - spreading northeastward into southeast OK and western AR. A very unstable air mass is present in this region, and the potential exists for a cluster of multicell storms capable of damaging wind gusts and some hail.

sections.title: Western OK into KS
sections.text: The southern fringe of stronger southwesterly midlevel winds have overspread western OK. A weak surface front extends from the eastern TX panhandle, across northwest OK, into central KS. This boundary will likely be the focus for scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms. High CAPE values and sufficient shear will result in multicell and a few supercell storms capable of damaging winds and large hail.

sections.title: Eastern CO and Western KS
sections.text: Low-level winds are forecast to back and become more southeasterly later this afternoon and evening over parts of eastern CO, enhancing upslope flow and helping to destabilize the air mass. A shortwave trough over UT will rotate into southeast CO, resulting in scattered thunderstorms over the mountains - spreading into the plains later today. Strong shear profiles and sufficient CAPE will support a risk of severe storms capable of hail and damaging winds. Activity should develop into western KS later tonight. ..Hart/Karstens.. 06/22/2019

outlooks.summary: Clusters of thunderstorms will remain capable of producing severe weather over parts of the central and southern Plains today, as well as from the mid Mississippi Valley across parts of the Southeast.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: No appreciable changes to the outlook areas are being implemented at this time, as forecast reasoning remains valid. Storms -- and some severe risk -- continue over a large portion of the Mid South and Southeast, while convection is now on the increase across the central and southern Plains region. This is all in line with prior forecast expectations, and thus only minor line tweaks -- reflective of current convective trends, appear necessary. ..Goss.. 06/22/2019 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1119 AM CDT Sat Jun 22 2019/

outlooks.summary: Clusters of thunderstorms will remain capable of producing severe weather over parts of the central and southern Plains today, as well as from the mid Mississippi Valley across parts of the Southeast.

sections.title: Southern and Central Plains/Lower Missouri Valley
sections.text: The latest water vapor imagery shows southwest mid-level flow over the southern and central Plains with a shortwave trough embedded in the flow over Oklahoma and Kansas. An MCS is ongoing just ahead of this feature from northwest Oklahoma into east-central Kansas along the western edge of a pocket of strong instability. Near the max in instability in southeast Kansas, the RAP is showing MLCAPE values as high as 4,500 J/kg. In addition, the Topeka WSR-88D VWP has 0-6 km shear near 40 kt with some directional shear in the low to mid-levels. This should continue to be favorable for supercells with large hail. Very large hail will be possible from near Wichita northeastward to near the Kansas City Metro along the axis of strongest instability. As the MCS continues to grow upscale, the wind damage threat should gradually increase as well. Further to the northeast into northwestern Missouri and southern Iowa, a very moist airmass is in place with surface dewpoints in the lower 70s F. This is contributing to strong instability with the RAP showing MLCAPE values in the 2,500 to 3,500 J/kg range. Surface winds across this area are backed to the east which is contributing to moderate deep-la

sections.title: Southeast Colorado/Western Kansas
sections.text: The latest water vapor imagery shows an upper-level trough over the Intermountain West with southwest mid-level flow located in the southern and central Rockies into the central High Plains. A cluster of strong thunderstorms is ongoing ahead of the trough in southeast Colorado along a zone of low-level convergence east of the Sangre de Cristos. This activity should move eastward across southeast Colorado and into southwestern Kansas late this evening. As the cluster of storms interacts with somewhat stronger instability across southwestern Kansas, the severe threat should continue into the overnight period. Isolated large hail and wind damage will be possible with the stronger storms.

sections.title: Southeast
sections.text: Several clusters of strong to severe storms are currently ongoing from north-central Alabama eastward into Georgia. These storms are located in a moderately unstable airmass where the RAP is estimating MLCAPE values from 2,000 to 3,000 J/kg. This combined with steep low-level lapse rates will continue to support isolated severe storm development this evening. The storms will continue to move east-southeastward across the Southeast for a couple more hours and be accompanied by a wind-damage threat. ..Broyles.. 06/23/2019

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms are expected to increase in coverage and intensity through early afternoon, gradually developing into southeast-moving clusters of storms with a risk for damaging winds and isolated large hail. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed prior to 18Z/2 pm EDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: a frontal boundary extends west from near the NC/SC border at 1630Z into a remnant convective system over eastern TN. A separate diffuse outflow boundary extended across southern SC west across northeast GA. Downstream of the TN convective system, substantial diabatic heating of a very moist air mass (upper 60s/lower 70s dew points) is underway. The region lies beneath the eastern fringe of an EML that will contribute to strong surface-based instability this afternoon with SBCAPE in excess of 2000 J/kg over much of the area. As CINH continues to erode, thunderstorms are expected to develop/increase in coverage this afternoon near the aforementioned boundaries and along the leading edge of the convective system. The combination of steep low-level lapse rates, water-loading in updrafts and mid-level drying evident on forecast soundings will result in a risk for damaging winds with the strongest storms. Evolution towards southeast-moving clusters given 25-30 kts of northwesterly mid-level flow is expected with time resulting in corridors of more concentrated damaging wind risk. The combination of strong low-level lapse rates and instability, boundary interaction and tendency for upscale growth with time suggests some potential for transient low-level circulations to develop, possibly resulting in a brief tornado. Despite marginal deep-layer shear, the steep mid-level lapse rates will also contribute to isolated instances of large hail. Convective trends are being monitored and a Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed prior to 18Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Convective development is likely this afternoon downstream of ongoing MCV. Area is being monitored for possible watch issuance by mid-afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Regional mesoanalysis/visible satellite shows a remnant MCV and associated mid-level cloud cover over portions of central/northern Texas, drifting northeastward. Along the eastern periphery of this feature, strong diabatic heating has allowed temperatures to warm quickly into the low 90s F along with steepening low-level lapse rates (near 8 C/km). With dew point temperatures in the upper 60s and low 70s F, a very unstable airmass is present downstream of the MCV, with MLCAPE values of 3000+ J/kg over much of eastern/northeastern Texas and eastern Oklahoma. While deep-layer shear is meager at best (generally < 20 kt effective bulk shear) over the region, forecast soundings indicate the potential for localized MCV-related enhancement to the shear profile, perhaps approaching 30-35 kt, particularly over north Texas into southern Oklahoma later this afternoon. While several uncertainties remain regarding convective development and the ensuing evolution, the current expectation is for a cluster or two of multi-cellular storms to develop, arcing along the eastern periphery of the ongoing MCV. In addition, other storms may spontaneously develop over southeast Oklahoma/far western Arkansas as convective temperatures are eclipsed. This scenario is supported by convection-allowing guidance (latest HRRR/HREF solutions). Storms that develop will pose a threat for severe hail and gusty outflow winds, given the aforementioned environmental conditions. Perhaps the greatest uncertainty at this time is the extent/coverage of storms that develop, and whether or not storms can develop a coherent cold pool and grow upscale. Thus, the area will continue to be monitored for the possibility of watch issuance by mid-afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms should increase in intensity this afternoon with a risk primarily for damaging winds. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch is possible prior to 3 pm CDT/20Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A long-lived convective complex continues to move southeast at 30 kts across southeast MO/western KY at 19Z, with a well-established cold pool and substantial downstream heating/destabilization. Despite rather weak deep-layer shear, current expectations are for the leading edge convection to intensify over the next couple of hours with an increasing risk for damaging winds given strong to extreme instability and DCAPE in excess of 1000 J/kg. Convective trends will continue to be monitored and a Severe Thunderstorm Watch is possible prior to 20Z/3 pm CDT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Widespread convective development expected this afternoon, with large hail/damaging wind gusts the primary threats. Watch likely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite shows a northward advancing area of developing cumulus, associated with low-level moisture advection, over southern/southeastern Kansas into far west-central Missouri, beneath a broken layer of northeastward streaming mid-level cloud cover. Some vertical development in the low-level clouds can be noted along the stalled frontal boundary oriented from northwest Oklahoma/Texas Panhandle into northeast Kansas, particularly near an analyzed meso-low over central Kansas, and along the edge of a modified cold pool from an overnight/morning MCS, stretching from west-central to far southern Missouri. Surface temperatures have warmed into the upper 80s F within the warm sector, where dew point temperatures are in the low to mid 70s F. Consequently, the atmosphere is undergoing rapid destabilization, where MLCAPE values are now exceeding 3000 J/kg. As the area continues to destabilize, widespread convective development is anticipated over the region within the next few hours, particularly along the aforementioned baroclinic zones initially. Effective bulk shear of 35-40 kt is common across the region (lessening with southward extent), and should help to organize the convection into multicellular/supercellular structures capable of large hail and damaging wind gusts. Watch issuance can be expected soon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Increasing coverage/intensity of convection likely this afternoon as storms approach the Front Range. Area being monitored for possible watch issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Regional mesoanalysis depicts a well-defined mid-level short-wave trough over central Colorado advancing steadily eastward. This feature is providing the impetus for large-scale forcing for ascent that, along with cold-air advection aloft, has led to modest destabilization over central Colorado amidst shallow/meager low-level moisture over the central Rockies. Consequently, scattered/marginal convection has developed over the region that is now approaching the Front Range. Meanwhile, surface winds along and east of the Front Range are acquiring more of an easterly/upslope component in response to the approaching short wave. As convection propagates eastward and into the lower-terrain areas along and east of the Front Range, storms are expected to intensify as they encounter richer boundary-layer moisture and greater instability (MLCAPE 1000-1500 J/kg). These storms should acquire supercell characteristics, given ample effective bulk shear (45-50 kt), posing a threat for mainly large hail and damaging wind gusts. Convective trends will continue to be monitored for possible watch issuance by late afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk for mainly damaging winds and isolated instances of large hail continues across the watch area.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Severe thunderstorms were in progress at 2030Z across northwest SC/south-central North Carolina in association with a long-lived southeast-moving convective system. Radar reflectivity from KGSP and KCAE show a continued strengthening of leading edge updrafts, suggesting the damaging wind/isolated large hail risk will continue as the line moves southeast along an instability gradient into the early evening. Farther south across the watch area, thunderstorms over eastern GA/southern SC have merged into a mix of clusters and short line segments while generally moving east. Strong surface-based instability and steep low-level lapse rates will result in a continued risk for damaging winds and perhaps severe hail as storms move across eastern GA and the SC Low Country. ..Bunting.. 06/22/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The greatest severe threat is confined to southern and eastern portions of WW 425. Local spatial extensions may be needed in downstream areas of east-central AL/west-central GA pending convective trends.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Widespread areas of convective overturning have stabilized portions of central AL upstream of a weakly organized linear complex over Clay/Randolph/Tallapoosa counties. Ahead of this complex, strong instability persists within a weakly sheared environment, with the greatest severe threat tied to updrafts along/near the leading edge of this complex. As southeastward forward propagation continues, the storms may eventually reach the southern extent of WW 424 with some risk for damaging wind gusts. This may necessitate spatial extensions of WW 425 into Lee AL and Muscogee/Harris GA and vicinity over the next 1-2 hours. Farther west, new updrafts have been developing along and near an outflow boundary that extends westward into Tuscaloosa and Lamar counties in AL. These storms will pose a brief wind-damage threat over the next few hours. In far southern Middle Tennessee, another linear complex is organizing and moving southward into northern Alabama. While the proximity of a mid-level shortwave and moderate instability was likely supporting this development, the downstream airmass has been overturned by prior convection. An isolated severe risk will likely exist with this activity pending further organization, though this risk will likely be too low to necessitate another WW issuance. ..Cook.. 06/22/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A conditional severe threat will likely persist into this evening across a small part of the eastern TX Panhandle vicinity into western OK. If a storm develops, large hail and strong wind gusts would be possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An isolated severe threat may persist into this evening across the far eastern TX Panhandle into western OK in the vicinity of a surface trough. Severe storms have developed along the surface trough further to the northeast across northwest OK into south-central KS in WW 426. Conditions are more marginal to the southwest across the MCD area where capping is somewhat stronger. Surface dewpoints are about 5-10 degrees F lower as well, though still in the mid to upper 60s F. A couple of tries at convective initiation have been noted near Donley County TX to the northwest of CDS and cumulus across the area appears to be deepening modestly. Also evident in visible satellite as well as radar loops are a couple of westward advancing boundaries, perhaps outflow or gravity waves associated with the MCV near the Red River/SPS. It is uncertain if these boundaries will have a negative or positive impact on convective initiation. If a storm is able to develop though, it will have 1500-2500 J/kg MLCAPE and 30-40 kt effective shear to aid in storm organization. Furthermore, a southerly low level jet is expected to increase this evening and this could further aid in severe potential with mainly large hail and strong wind gusts the main concern. At this time, the threat appears conditional and would likely remain isolated to a couple of storms. If convection does develop WFO OUN would be able to aerially extend WW 426 across western OK, but a watch may not be issued across the small portions of WFOs AMA and/or LUB that would potentially be impacted. ..Leitman.. 06/22/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated threat for damaging wind and hail will persist for the next couple of hours, though a WW issuance probably will not be needed.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A couple of areas remain a focus for convection across the discussion area - one from near NQA eastward to just north of MSL associated with a remnant outflow boundary and another near/just east of UOX. Though instability within the pre-convective airmass is relatively strong, weak shear is causing many of these updrafts to be undercut by cool near-surface outflow, limiting the longevity of any severe threat. Still, a few storms will contain an hail/wind risk over the next hour or two - especially north through northwest of MSL. A WW issuance is not anticipated for this activity. ..Cook.. 06/22/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat persists across remaining portions of WW 424.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Severe potential continues along the leading edge of a couple of mature cold pools - one located from S of FAY to E of OGB, and another extending from E of OGB to near CHS and adjacent coastal waters. Updrafts continue to propagate on the leading edge of the cold pools and will continue to pose a risk for damaging wind and large hail given strong pre-convective, surface-based instability and modest mid-level westerly flow/shear. This threat should persist southeastward through coastal areas and adjacent waters over the next 1-2 hours. Upstream from this activity, convective overturning and low-level stabilization should allow for a decreased severe threat, with those portions of WW 424 being canceled before the scheduled expiration time of 01Z. ..Cook.. 06/22/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A damaging wind threat will continue across north-central OK into central and eastern KS and parts of western/northern MO this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several lines and clusters of thunderstorms are ongoing this evening across northwest OK, central and eastern KS and northwest MO. Some hints of better organization into a forward propagating line/bowing segment are apparent across parts of central into northeast KS to the west of Topeka and Kansas City. Cold pool generation with temperatures in the mid 60s to low 70s were noted behind the line of storms across north-central KS with some indications of a rear-inflow jet based on lower reflectivity returns behind the developing apex of the bow near Manhattan, KS. In fact, estimated winds near 60 mph and some minor wind damage has been reported in this vicinity. Further south, a line of storms extended from near Wichita southwestward into northwest OK. Wind gusts of 60-70 mph and 1 inch diameter hail have been reported with these storms. A third line of storms across north-central MO also showed signs of more organized forward propagation as it tracks eastward at around 40-50 mph. Estimated gusts to 60 mph and minor damage was also occurring with this line. Guidance has not performed overly well in depicting ongoing convection and therefore evolution of storms is a bit uncertain. However, an increasing low level jet through the evening will support continued organized severe convection into the nighttime hours. To add to the complexity of convective evolution overnight, an MCV is tracking north/northeast across central into northern OK. What role this feature may play also remains unclear. What seems to be a reasonable expectation is that one or more bowing segments/forward propagating clusters will spread eastward across eastern KS into western MO where 00z RAOBs from TOP and SGF show an uncapped, strongly unstable, steep lapse rate environment. mesoscale_discussions.summary: An organized cluster of strong to severe storms has increased forward speed and will approach the southern extent of WW 425 over the next hour. A new downstream WW is being considered.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An ongoing cluster of severe storms just south of Macon, GA has organized into a forward-propagating linear complex while accelerating southeastward along a remnant outflow boundary from an earlier MCS now over GA/SC coastal waters. These storms continue to migrate into a strongly unstable airmass characterized by 3000-4000 J/kg SBCAPE, which should continue to support a hail and wind-damage threat as storms continue to move southward - especially if they retain organization. These storms will approach the southern extent of WW 425 over the next 1-2 hours, though concerns exist regarding interactions with downstream convection just ahead of the complex. If these storms can maintain their organization and severity, a new downstream Severe Thunderstorm Watch may be needed.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Damaging wind and hail threat will continue across portions of WW 428. A downstream watch may be needed in the next couple of hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convection across southeast CO has become better organized this evening as it tracks eastward toward southwest KS. Additional storms have developed southwestward into northeast NM as well. A surface low was noted in surface analysis across northeast NM with a dryline extending southward through eastern NM and a weak surface trough/confluence zone extending eastward from the low across the northern TX Panhandle. Further east, a segmented cold front/composite outflow was located across central KS and far northwest OK. Latest HRRR guidance suggests the complex of storms across southeast CO/northeast NM will continue to shift east/southeast in the vicinity of low level easterly flow and lobe of modest instability/increasing effective shear across southwest KS into the OK and northern TX Panhandles. Increasing forcing for ascent, associated with vort max ejecting across NM, is evident in water vapor imagery. This is further supported by isolated severe storms that have developed across parts of the TX Panhandle and Texas South Plains regions in the last hour or so. This stronger forcing should further aid continuation/organization of eastward propagating storms. As such, a new watch may be needed downstream of WW 428 in the next couple of hours, as a damaging wind and hail threat could persist east/southeastward into the overnight hours. ..Leitman.. 06/23/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong gusts will continue to be a concern across WW 429 the next couple of hours. The overall threat should diminish with south and eastward extent across MO after 06z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Portions of a line of convection extending from north-central MO into southeast KS has become re-invigorated to the southeast of the Kansas City metro area in the vicinity of Johnson, Henry and Bates Counties MO. A 73 mph wind gust was measured within the past 30 min in Johnson County with other strong gusts around 35-45 kt noted elsewhere. A southeastward surge in the line is clearly apparent in radar loops over the past hour or two and the EAX VWP shows a 45-60 kt descending rear-inflow jet. Strong, locally damaging winds likely will continue with this portion of the line as it tracks southeast toward portions of southwest and central MO. That being said, the overall threat should diminish with southeastward extent as instability wanes and inhibition increases toward the I-44 corridor in MO. It is possible that some threat could develop further east along the I-70 corridor into northeast/east-central MO but effective shear weakens considerably across this area and an overall weakening trend should occur downstream of WW 429. ..Leitman.. 06/23/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for hail and strong wind gusts continues across much of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 430. A downstream watch will likely be needed across south-central KS and western/northern OK soon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The initially discrete storms in southeastern CO have undergone a linear transition and cold pool amalgamation. Convective initiation has also occurred along the southward-surging portion of the cold pool in the OK and northern TX Panhandles. These storms have led to a somewhat messy convective structure. Even so, continued organization into a linear MCS is anticipated, with a eastward/east-southeastward motion thereafter. The downstream air mass across south-central KS and western OK supports a continued severe threat into these areas and downstream watch is likely. Farther south, discrete supercell over Wheeler County Texas continues to have a very strong updraft, with 60+ dBz noted over 30 kft. While low-level nocturnal stabilization will continue, well-organized character to the ongoing supercell combined with steep mid-level lapse rates and strong buoyancy suggest storm persistence and a downstream severe threat into central portions of western OK.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for damaging wind gusts and isolated hail continues across Severe Thunderstorm Watch 431.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several bowing line segments are currently moving through Severe Thunderstorm Watch 431. The northernmost bowing segment is currently moving eastward through south-central KS at around 40 kt, although some discrete propagation may have occurred recently as the line intersected preceding storms. Primary threat with this bowing segment is damaging wind gusts, although the recent merger with preceding storms has acting to increase updraft strength with a resulting increase in threat for large hail. Subsequent storm mergers farther east will likely have the same effect. A second bowing line segment is moving east-northeastward into northwest OK at 45 kt. Orthogonal orientation of the storm motion to the shear vector and favorable location within the instability gradient suggests the environment supports storm persistence. That being said, the northern portion of this line has recently surged forward, suggesting the updraft may have collapsed. Decreasing echo tops add merit to this scenario. ..Mosier.. 06/23/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for brief tornadoes and isolated damaging wind gusts exists across central AR. Convective trends are being monitored for possible watch issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Surface analysis places an outflow boundary from roughly 20 mi west of ARG (in northeast AR) southwestward to about 25 mi north of LIT and then back westward to FSM. Precipitation has been ongoing most of the night north of this boundary, with warm mid-level temperatures and poor mid-level lapse rates as result. However, south of this boundary, the air mass is characterized by temperatures in the 80s, dewpoints in the mid 70s, and strong buoyancy. A few thunderstorms have recently developed south of the boundary (in the Polk/Scott/Logan County AR vicinity) and subsequently moved northeastward over the boundary, experiencing updraft intensification/rotation as they do. This rotation has been short-lived as the updrafts weaken in the more stable air north of the outflow. The persistence of this pattern is uncertain, but given the recent trends and persistence of favorable vertical vorticity along the boundary, convective trends are being monitored closely. A watch may be needed if more development south of the boundary appears imminent, supporting a longer-lived tornado threat.
